articles.title: MAGA is ending. In conservative circles, the debate over what comes next is heating up. - The Boston Globe
articles.excerpt: The below-the-radar fight over the future of the Republican Party will have enormous consequences for the country.
articles.content:
Peter Laffin is a senior editor at the Washington Examiner.

Left-of-center news outlets have spent the past decade asking readers to consider how the “MAGA base” of the Republican Party feels about any given story.

How is Trump’s war in Iran playing with the MAGA base? Is the MAGA base upset about the lack of transparency on the Epstein files? Who is the MAGA base’s preferred candidate for 2028?

But all variations of this question are growing obsolete. MAGA is a declining force in electoral politics.

Polling data suggests that MAGA is shrinking as a percentage of the Republican electorate. It’s no coincidence that the faction is fading as the Trump era fades; Trump holds the faction together, not ideology.

There will be no MAGA faction without him. No one will “inherit” his movement.

And with Trump’s exit looming, a fierce battle over the future of the Republican Party is underway.

As a senior editor at a center-right news outlet, the Washington Examiner, I’m intensely interested in this factional struggle for control of the GOP — one playing out in real time, mostly outside the spotlight of the daily political press.

To that end, I’ve spent the past several months running a think tank symposium series featuring essays by the most influential intellectuals representing the many factions of conservative policy. Over four installments, the series — titled “Right Way Forward” — has served as a forum for the most consequential debates of the looming post-Trump conservative movement.

So far I’ve commissioned and edited more than 50 essays from the biggest names in conservative policy. They argue passionately about the state’s role in the economy, the true nature of American national identity, and the United States’ role in the world.

Everyone involved understands the once-in-a-generation opportunity in front of them, and they are fighting with everything they’ve got to advance their agenda and secure influence in the post-Trump GOP.

The outcome of that fight will have enormous consequences for the party — and for the country.

A coalition of convenience

Democrats have always struggled to understand the MAGA phenomenon: what it was, why it happened, what it meant. This partly explains their inability to defeat it — and why they are already struggling to position themselves against what is forming in its wake.

On the left, the term “MAGA base” is often used as a rhetorical prop — turning the movement into a caricature that fails to communicate much of value. This exercise made progressively less sense as Trump’s coalition grew more diverse, culminating in 2024 when Trump won roughly half of the nation’s Latino voters and a clear majority of the working class — many of them former Obama voters who’d crossed over in 2016 and never crossed back.

One reason MAGA was so difficult to define was that its followers had little in common beyond a favorable view of the Trump political project. Hawks and isolationists. Free marketeers and protectionists. Deficit hawks and pro-entitlement populists. Pro-family Christians and tech-right libertarians. Factory workers and corporate executives. MAGA contained all of this.

Faced with a coalition that made so little intuitive sense, the left reached for the simplest explanation: that MAGA was a cult of personality.

There was some truth to that. A certain element on the right continues to afford Trump a highly intense and uncritical loyalty. They often appear less like political followers than disciples — even when, perhaps especially when, his worst impulses surface.

But this faction was never as large as Trump and his adversaries suggested it was — each for its own reasons. For Trump, a fanatical following was proof of his strength: A leader who commands blind loyalty seems more powerful than one who commands mere political support.

For his adversaries, it was both a mobilizing tool and fund-raising gold. Democrats came to rely heavily on the specter of a radicalized MAGA movement and ran campaigns organized more around alarm than affordability or fixing the border. The unrelenting focus on the threat of MAGA came at the expense of developing a compelling policy agenda — a failure that lingers as the socialist wing remakes the party in its own image.

So if not a cohesive ideological coalition or a cult of personality, what was MAGA?

It was, to use a Trump word, something of a deal — an alliance of convenience, not conviction, between a man and a growing chunk of the country that had come to despise the ruling Establishment for squandering a generation of American prosperity, power, and social cohesion.

They didn’t all love Trump. A meaningful share of his 2024 coalition didn’t even like him. A September 2024 CBS News/YouGov poll found that among voters who disliked him personally, 21 percent would vote for him anyway — four times the rate of Harris dislikers who still backed her.

They didn’t vote for him out of love or loyalty but because they believed the former businessman would tame inflation and improve the economy. And they hoped he would strike a blow at the political and media Establishment while he was at it.

The war on inflation hasn’t gone very well. But Trump does have the old guard on the left and right wandering in a kind of exile.

That isn’t to say voters are happy with his efforts to replace them. Today, Trump’s approval ratings hover around 40 percent, and approval ratings for his key initiatives — the Iran war, tariffs, and mass deportations — are even more dismal. Trump’s second term has been unpopular and disorienting, characterized by an incoherent whipsaw agenda with no fixed moral or intellectual center.

Would Americans restore the old Establishment if given the chance? Maybe, maybe not. Approval ratings for the institutions Trump has steamrolled continue to run far beneath his.

Trump’s exit — and yes, he will leave the stage for good no later than January 2029 — will leave a hole in American politics that only a handful of presidents have ever left: Theodore Roosevelt, Franklin Roosevelt, figures who so thoroughly dominated the national psyche that politics simply couldn’t be imagined without them until it had to be.

Both parties are having an identity crisis as a result. One built itself around Trump, the other built itself entirely around opposing him. Without him, both parties are staring into the same void.

The new GOP

A variety of factions are fighting to define the post-Trump GOP. Their differences are rarely tactical or strategic — they are over principles and aims.

Take the issue of national identity. On one side are the “creedalists” — especially scholars from the American Enterprise Institute — who believe the United States is fundamentally a creedal nation, founded primarily on the principles enumerated in the Declaration of Independence.

On the other side are the “particularists” — represented by scholars from the Heritage Foundation and the Claremont Institute — who say America is more than an idea on a page. Rather, it’s a particular people with a shared history, culture, and often faith. Reduce America to a creed, they argue, and you get a country with no reason to hold together at all.

These visions are not merely opposed but irreconcilable. And the stakes couldn’t be higher: From whichever principle wins out, highly consequential policies will flow, particularly related to immigration. If the particularists win, immigration ceases to be a question of assimilability and becomes one of cultural compatibility — thereby justifying sharp cuts to legal admissions, longer naturalization periods, stricter assimilation requirements.

There’s an equally fierce fight shaping up over the size and shape of government in the economy. The free marketeers of the Cato Institute and Advancing American Freedom, former vice president Mike Pence’s rapidly growing upstart, maintain that markets, not Washington, should still allocate capital and labor. Meanwhile, economic nationalists in the mold of the America First Policy Institute and Vice President JD Vance believe that the economy is “rigged,” requiring state intervention through tariffs, industrial policy, and antitrust action against Big Tech.

Vance, the current favorite to carry the Republican torch in 2028, has cited Elizabeth Warren and Bernie Sanders as his “favorite Democrats on policy outcomes” and argued in his new book that the gross domestic product is a “useless statistic” — that it elevates economic growth above dignity, community, and other moral goods.

As with national identity, the competing views here are mutually exclusive. And without a Trump-like figure to unite these factions, only one side’s vision will win out.

It’s much the same with foreign policy. The Iran war has only deepened the existing divide between those who believe America should uphold its traditional role as guarantor of global order and those who advocate for retreating from foreign entanglements. The sheer bitterness of this dispute, sharpest where it touches the alliance with Israel, was on full display when Trump’s own allies argued over whether the short-lived cease-fire with Iran was a victory or a betrayal.

So what will the post-MAGA Republican Party look like?

We sit at an exhilarating and crucial moment in our political history precisely because it could go either way. The debate is genuinely open and the momentum shifts from one news cycle to the next. The nationalist populists enjoy the advantage of having their man a heartbeat from the presidency and the current polling front-runner for the nomination. The traditional conservatives, now playing the role of the rebellious outsiders, enjoy the advantage of a Republican primary electorate that has never actually voted to abolish the free market, retreat from the global stage, or trade the founding creed for a narrower definition of national identity.

Democrats would do well to watch this fight closely. They spent 10 years trying, and largely failing, to beat a personality. They are about to face an argument. They do not yet know which one they’ll be facing.

And as they learned with Donald Trump, you cannot beat what you refuse to take seriously — let alone what you don’t understand.

articles.title: John Galliano's Met Gala exhibit canceled amid backlash
articles.excerpt: The Met's decision to highlight the work by designer John Galliano sparked widespread controversy due to his history of antisemitic and racist comments.
articles.content:
Updated on: August 31, 2026 / 9:22 AM EDT / CBS News

Designer John Galliano and the Metropolitan Museum of Art in New York City say the planned exhibition highlighting his work in conjunction with the 2027 Met Gala will not be going forward, following weeks of backlash.

The designer said in a social media post on Monday that after "much reflection and discussion, with all those involved, I've decided, with great sadness, that it is best for the exhibition not to take place at this time." The Met confirmed in a statement that the "Spring 2027 exhibition devoted to his four-decade oeuvre will not proceed as planned."

The decision to highlight the work by Galliano, who is known for his theatrical and dramatic designs, sparked widespread controversy earlier this month due to his history of antisemitic and racist comments. These remarks led to his dismissal from Christian Dior in 2011 and a hate crime conviction in France. 

"I remain fully accountable for the pain caused by my words in the past, particularly the hurt I caused to the Jewish and Asian communities, and I remain deeply sorry," Galliano said in his statement on Monday.

The Met said it will announce details on a new spring Costume Institute exhibition and the 2027 Met Gala at a later date.

articles.excerpt: Goalie says with training camp approaching, moving on from Winnipeg 'best path forward'
articles.content:
Goalie says with training camp approaching, moving on from Winnipeg 'best path forward'

© Sam Hodde/Getty Images

Connor Hellebuyck has made public his desire to be traded by the Winnipeg Jets.

The three-time winner of the Vezina Trophy, which is awarded to the best goalie in the NHL, said in a statement on Thursday that he privately requested a trade “several months ago" but is now making it public with NHL training camps set to open on Sept. 16. 

"I have tried to handle the situation quietly and respectfully while giving the organization time to explore its options,” Hellebuyck said in the statement released by his agent, Ray Petkau. "With training camp approaching, I felt it was important to publicly confirm my request. My position has not changed. I believe moving on is the best path forward for me and my family."

The Jets will play their first preseason game on Sept. 19. Their first regular-season game is against the Boston Bruins at Canada Life Centre on Oct. 2.

Statement from Connor Hellebuyck: pic.twitter.com/hW8sNw1LJi

— Ray Petkau (@RayPetkau) August 27, 2026

Statement from Connor Hellebuyck: pic.twitter.com/hW8sNw1LJi

Hellebuyck, who helped the United States win the gold medal at the 2026 Milano Cortina Olympics, was 23-23-11 with a 2.86 goals-against average and .895 save percentage in 57 NHL games last season. Winnipeg (35-35-12) finished eight points behind the Los Angeles Kings for the second wild card into the Stanley Cup Playoffs from the Western Conference.

After the season, Hellebuyck had this to say about the Jets and their ability to win the Stanley Cup: 

“It’s hard. It’s hard. Can you get the pieces that you need? Will the players come? These are always questions that you have in Winnipeg,” he said on April 18. “I’ve made it my home and I like it here, but the majority of the League doesn’t feel the same way.”

On June 26, Jets general manager Kevin Cheveldayoff said Winnipeg was listening to trade offers for Hellebuyck, but he did not provide a definitive answer as to whether his franchise goalie had requested a move.

“Certainly, as an organization we're going to listen,” Cheveldayoff said. “Everyone saw (Hellebuyck’s) press conference at the end of the year. He was passionate. Certainly, in our exit meetings we had some frank conversations as well, but again, what happens in those meetings certainly stays private.”

In response to his goaltender's public request on Thursday, Cheveldayoff said: "Connor has been open with us about his desire for a change. He has been an important part of the Winnipeg Jets organization for many years, and we have tremendous respect for what he has accomplished here. While we will continue to work through the situation in a thoughtful manner, there is no update at this time."

Statement in response to Connor Hellebuyck’s request for a trade. pic.twitter.com/plv5xH92M4

— Winnipeg Jets (@NHLJets) August 27, 2026

Statement in response to Connor Hellebuyck’s request for a trade. pic.twitter.com/plv5xH92M4

Hellebuyck has been one of the best goalies in the NHL since he entered the League during the 2015-16 season. 

In 2024-25, he had his best individual season, going 47-12-3 with a 2.00 GAA, .925 save percentage and eight shutouts in 63 games. He won the Hart Trophy as the NHL's most valuable player, the Vezina Trophy for the third time, and helped the Jets win the Presidents' Trophy as the team with the League's best record (56-22-4).

Hellebuyck, 33, is entering the third season of a seven-year, $59.5 million contract ($8.5 million average annual value) he signed on Oct. 9, 2023.

He has played his entire 11-season NHL career for Winnipeg, which selected him in the fifth round (No. 130) of the 2012 NHL Draft. Since entering the League, he leads goalies in games played (625) and starts (615), and is second in wins (345). Among goalies to play at least 300 games during that span, his .916 save percentage is third, and his 2.58 GAA is tied for seventh.

Hellebuyck is one of four goalies, along with Dominik Hasek, Martin Brodeur and Patrick Roy, to win the Vezina Trophy at least three times (2019-20, 2023-24, 2024-25) since NHL general managers began voting on the award in 1981.

The Jets signed goalie Stuart Skinner to a two-year, $7.5 million contract ($3.75 million AAV) on July 1. Their top goalie prospect, Domenic DiVincentiis, was 13-16-2 with a 3.03 GAA and .896 save percentage in 34 games with Manitoba of the American Hockey League last season. The 22-year-old has yet to play in the NHL. 

"I appreciate everything Winnipeg Jets fans have meant to me throughout my career and hope a resolution can be reached soon," Hellebuyck said.

articles.title: Jets star goalie Connor Hellebuyck confirms trade request
articles.excerpt: Three-time Vezina Trophy-winning goaltender Connor Hellebuyck publicly confirmed Thursday that he asked the Winnipeg Jets to trade him.
articles.content:
WINNIPEG, Manitoba -- Three-time Vezina Trophy-winning goaltender Connor Hellebuyck publicly confirmed Thursday that he asked the Winnipeg Jets to trade him.

In a statement released by his agent, Ray Petkau, Hellebuyck said he made the request several months ago and "tried to handle the situation quietly and respectfully while giving the organization time to explore its options."

Hellebuyck said he felt it was important to go public because training camp is fast approaching. Camps are set to open in roughly three weeks.

"My position has not changed, and I believe moving on is the best path forward for me and my family," Hellebuyck said. "(I) hope a resolution can be reached soon."

Hellebuyck, 33, has played his entire NHL career with the Jets and was voted MVP in the 2024-25 season. He backstopped the U.S. to the gold medal at the Olympics in February.

A team spokesperson did not immediately respond to a message seeking comment.

Trade rumors swirled about Hellebuyck in late June around the draft, but nothing came to fruition. The Michigan native missed time because of injury and had a career-worst .895 save percentage last season as Winnipeg underachieved expectations and missed the playoffs.

But his track record and body of work are among the best at the position over the past decade. His 345 wins, 2.58 goals-against average and .916 save percentage since entering the league in 2015 are second only to Tampa Bay two-time Stanley Cup champion Andrei Vasilevskiy.

Hellebuyck has not enjoyed the same postseason success as Vasilevskiy and the Lightning. He's 24-34, with the Jets only making it past the second round and into the Western Conference final once, back in 2018.

He signed an eight-year, $59.5 million extension with Winnipeg in October 2023. He's under contract through 2031 at a salary cap hit of $8.5 million.

"Winnipeg has been my home for my entire NHL career, and I will always be grateful for my time there," Hellebuyck said. "I appreciate everything Winnipeg Jets fans have meant to me throughout my career."

articles.title: Connor Hellebuyck trade fits: 8 teams that could make a deal with the Jets
articles.excerpt: Winnipeg doesn't seem likely to enter a full rebuild, so what does that mean for the possible return on Hellebuyck?
articles.content:
NHL Offseason

Which teams make sense for a Connor Hellebuyck trade? Dilip Vishwanat / Getty Images

The top goalie in the world is hoping to be traded before NHL training camps open in September.

Connor Hellebuyck went public with his request to be traded from the Winnipeg Jets on Thursday. In a statement released by his agent, Ray Petkau, Hellebuyck confirmed that he asked for a trade from Winnipeg several months ago, and that he still believes moving on is the best path forward for him and his family. The Jets responded with a statement of their own from general manager Kevin Cheveldayoff, saying they will “continue to work through the situation in a thoughtful manner.”

The three-time Vezina Trophy-winning goaltender is hoping to find a new team sooner rather than later, while the Jets won’t be keen on moving their best player without receiving fair compensation. While we don’t know exactly what Winnipeg is asking for in return, here’s a summary from their perspective, from The Athletic’s Jets beat writer, Murat Ates:

“Winnipeg will seek to delay a rebuild if at all possible. Expect the Jets’ ideal return to focus on roster players – a top-six forward, a goaltender who can share the net with Skinner – and a first-round pick or similar asset. When Cheveldayoff named his team’s biggest needs, answering The Athletic’s question prior to the draft, he put his focus squarely on a second-line center. He then drafted Viggo Bjorck, who Winnipeg is inclined to give an NHL opportunity at 18 years old and who projects to be a strong two-way center. The selection doesn’t automatically pivot Winnipeg’s needs from center to right wing, where Gabriel Vilardi is the only surefire threat, but it gives the Jets options in terms of the forward they get back. Skinner has played at least 50 games for four straight seasons, so the Jets don’t need a surefire starter – just someone who can play a “1B” role and take 30 to 35 starts.”

The Athletic’s Chris Johnston reported on Thursday that one key difference between Hellebuyck’s trade request compared to others around the NHL is that he’s willing to waive his no-movement clause for a variety of teams, which means the Jets have options.

With that in mind, here are the teams that make the most sense as potential trade partners, and why some may be better fits than others.

Buffalo Sabres

Much of the conversation around potential landing spots for Hellebuyck has centered around Buffalo, and for good reason. The Sabres should be considered a frontrunner. They took a huge step forward in 2025-26, snapping a 14-year playoff drought. It was largely fueled by a top-five scoring attack, but they also received surprisingly steady goaltending from Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen and Alex Lyon, who combined to give them the third-highest team save percentage in the NHL.

It’s fair to wonder if the duo can repeat that in 2026-27. Luukkonen’s four full seasons in the NHL have bounced between stellar and disappointing, and Lyon’s career has been equally uneven.

With the talent the Sabres have at forward and on the blue line, Hellebuyck would instantly make them a top contender in the East. We’ve only seen Hellebuyck play behind a top-five scoring team twice in his career, and in both instances he led the NHL in wins. In 2017-18, he finished runner-up for the Vezina and led Winnipeg to the conference finals. In 2024-25, he helped the Jets win the Presidents’ Trophy and walked away with the Vezina and Hart trophies.

Buffalo’s salary cap situation is another reason to believe it’s a top landing spot. The Sabres still have $6.9 million in space, which is already nearly enough to fit Hellebuyck’s $8.5 million cap hit. If the Jets took Luukkonen back in a trade, it would clear another $4.75 million, leaving plenty of room. The Sabres also have a plethora of top-six forwards they could send Winnipeg’s way, including Josh Norris and Ryan McLeod, giving this potential trade a real chance.

Vegas Golden Knights

Rarely does a star player hit the trade market without the Golden Knights being mentioned in some capacity. Vegas has made multiple blockbuster trades over the last nine seasons, with several being under similar circumstances: a player unhappy in their current location.

General manager Kelly McCrimmon has made it clear that he’s happy with his current goalie tandem of Carter Hart and Adin Hill, but it doesn’t mean he won’t change his mind if the right opportunity presents itself. Neither Hart nor Hill was particularly impressive in the regular season, with the team ranking near the bottom of the league in save percentage and goals saved above expected. Hart was excellent in the playoffs, sans a poor ending in the Cup Final, and Hill has shown he is good enough to lead the team to a title, but Hellebuyck is obviously another tier of goalie entirely.

What makes this option particularly intriguing is the stylistic fit. Hellebuyck is a positional goalie who reads the play incredibly well and thrives in structure. Meanwhile, the Golden Knights defend with arguably the best structure in the NHL. They employ a zone defense that does an exceptional job of keeping the puck out of the high-danger areas and allows predictable shots. It’s why they led the league with the fewest high-danger chances and expected goals against last season.

Giving predictable chances to a goalie with Hellebuyck’s anticipation skills is a recipe for a fourth Vezina Trophy. The biggest hurdle in a trade between the Golden Knights and Jets would be cap space and trade assets. Vegas currently has only $1.9 million in space. If Hill and his $6.25 million cap hit were to be included in the return package, it would get Vegas close, but there’s no guarantee the Jets would be interested in taking on that contract for the next five years after Hill’s disappointing 2025-26 season.

The Golden Knights don’t have a first-round draft pick in next year’s draft, but they do have two in 2028 after acquiring one from the Rangers in the Pavel Dorofeyev trade this summer. If the Jets are looking for a top-six forward or top-four defenseman in return, Vegas is a bit handcuffed by no-trade clauses for most of its top players, but if there’s one thing we’ve learned, it’s that Vegas finds a way. From Hellebuyck’s perspective, Vegas’ consistent track record is appealing, as is joining Jack Eichel and Noah Hanifin, with whom he won a gold medal at the Olympics.

Carolina Hurricanes

Adding an elite goalie to the defending Stanley Cup champions would be bad news for the rest of the NHL, but is it realistic?

The Hurricanes have remained steadfast in their approach over the years, regularly passing on opportunities to add a high-dollar goalie and instead looking to find value in net while investing money elsewhere on the roster. It worked last season, as Frederik Andersen ($2.75 million cap hit) led them to the Cup Final, where Brandon Bussi (a waiver claim with a meager $775,000 cap hit) helped them win it all. Carolina is currently set up well to continue on that path, with Bussi signed for the next three seasons for $1.9 million per season, and Pyotr Kochetkov on an expiring deal worth only $2 million. That $3.9 million investment in goaltending is the third-lowest in the NHL.

General manager Eric Tulsky likely sees no reason to stray from this strategy, mere months after it won a championship, but it’s worth noting that under the quickly rising salary cap, Hellebuyck’s contract is arguably a value at this point. His cap hit accounts for only 8.2 percent of the total cap, which is closer to the deal Carolina signed Andersen to in 2021 (5.5 percent of the cap) than it is to the biggest goalie deals, such as the one Carey Price signed in Montreal in 2018, which accounted for 13.2 percent of the cap, or the one Sergei Bobrovsky signed in 2019 with Florida, which took up 12.3 percent of the cap.

It would be an against-the-grain move by the Hurricanes, but they have plenty of cap space and trade assets to make it happen if they chose to do so.

Utah Mammoth

The Mammoth could be a sneaky contender in this sweepstakes. They took major steps forward last season, pushed Vegas in the first round of the playoffs, and have several young players still on the way up. Karel Vejmelka has been solid in net, handling one of the biggest workloads of any goalie in the league over the last two seasons, but Hellebuyck obviously would be an upgrade.

The Jets may have no interest in trading their star goalie within the division, but Utah has plenty of future assets and top-six forwards to include in a potential trade if they did. The Mammoth don’t currently have quite enough cap space to fit in Hellebuyck, but they would if Vejmelka were included in the return package, and Winnipeg likely wouldn’t mind rolling with a duo of Vejmelka and Skinner.

If Winnipeg isn’t planning to enter a rebuild, helping a divisional opponent make the leap to true contender status doesn’t make much sense. Outside of that — which is admittedly a pretty big hurdle — Utah is an excellent fit for Hellebuyck.

New Jersey Devils

If newly appointed general manager Sunny Mehta wants to make a splash, this would certainly be it. His predecessor, Tom Fitzgerald, took a big swing at goalie by trading for Jacob Markstrom in 2024. After sending Markstrom and the remainder of his contract to Florida this summer, the Devils are left with a fairly bare cupboard in the crease.

Jake Allen and Nico Daws currently make up the cheapest goalie tandem in the NHL, with a combined cap hit of only $2.9 million. Allen has been excellent in his three seasons in New Jersey and is coming off arguably the best season of his 13-year NHL career, but he’s also 36 and hasn’t handled a true starter’s workload since 2018.

The Devils have been plagued by injuries the past few seasons, but there’s plenty of talent on the roster. With a little better luck in that department, and with elite goaltending, they could easily make the jump from lottery team to contender in the East.

San Jose Sharks

With one of the most exciting young rosters in the league, the Sharks seem primed for a breakout. Adding a world-class goalie would accelerate their timeline for contention in a big way, but it also feels like the timelines for Hellebuyck and the Sharks’ core don’t exactly match up.

San Jose finished in the bottom 10 last season in team save percentage, but that number is more of a product of abysmal defending than the goaltending itself. Yaroslav Askarov was inconsistent in his first year as a starter. He had stretches of brilliance, when he showed why he’s viewed as a franchise netminder. He had stretches when his game got a bit loose and too many pucks found the back of the net. Still, with a young team whose projected window to win isn’t quite open, it feels like allowing Askarov to grow as the true No. 1 is probably the better option.

If general manager Mike Grier wanted to add a stud veteran goalie to play alongside Askarov, he could’ve pursued Bobrovsky in free agency without having to trade anything, with the added benefit of adding a Russian legend for Askarov to learn from. He clearly feels comfortable with his current goalie room of Askarov, Alex Nedeljkovic and Eric Comrie.

From Winnipeg’s perspective, getting Askarov back in a trade would be fantastic. He’s only 24 and has Vezina-caliber potential if he reaches his ceiling, but considering the Sharks’ big-picture timeline, swapping the younger goalie for a more proven but aging Hellebuyck doesn’t seem prudent. There’s also no guarantee Hellebuyck includes the Sharks on his list of contenders he is willing to accept a trade to.

Columbus Blue Jackets

The Blue Jackets could be a dark horse in these sweepstakes. The fit isn’t obvious, considering they missed the playoffs for the sixth straight season last year and saw Jet Greaves emerge as one of the better young netminders in the league. Columbus currently ranks 20th in betting odds to win the Cup, and fifth to win their division, but a lot could change with an addition such as Hellebuyck.

The Blue Jackets were around league average in most statistics last season, but did allow the sixth-fewest high-danger chances, with a sturdy defense led by Hellebuyck’s Team USA teammate and Norris Trophy winner, Zach Werenski. If they get sizable leaps from young, talented forwards Adam Fantilli and Cole Sillinger, and the core of veterans up front plays to its potential, Columbus could be much improved. The team was red-hot under coach Rick Bowness before faltering down the stretch.

Columbus has plenty of cap space and a strong pool of young prospects to choose from in a potential trade. It’s not the most likely destination for Hellebuyck, but it wouldn’t be overly surprising to see Columbus take a big swing.

Dallas Stars

Is there potential for a blockbuster one-for-one goalie trade?

Hellebuyck wants to play for a contender, which Dallas clearly is. The Stars have been looking for something to get them over the hump, which Hellebuyck could clearly be. The Jets are hoping to acquire enough talent in this trade to avoid a full rebuild, and getting a younger, franchise goalie such as Jake Oettinger is probably the best they could ever hope for.

There’s just one major issue. Oettinger, who is signed through the 2032-33 season, has a full no-movement clause in his contract. The Lakeville, Minn., native loves Dallas and seemingly likely has no intention of waiving that clause, nor should he.

articles.title: FBI arrests fake 49er accused of scamming women out of $1.3 million via dating apps
articles.excerpt: Daejon Love allegedly formed fake relationships with women before pressuring them to send him thousands of dollars for fake investments.
articles.content:
Daejon Love and alleged accomplice Taylor Chan face charges of wire fraud and conspiracy to commit wire fraud. Samuel Corum / Getty Images

Two men, including one accused of posing as a San Francisco 49ers player, are under arrest for allegedly defrauding dozens of women out of more than $1.3 million in a scheme that lasted over four years.

The U.S. Attorney’s Office for Oregon said in an announcement that Daejon Labrayae Love, 35, and Taylor Jamie Chan, 18, targeted victims via dating apps and social media beginning in February 2022 and lasting through their arrest on Monday. They are each facing one count of wire fraud and two counts of conspiracy to commit wire fraud, all felonies. Investigators said they have identified 26 victims of the plot.

According to an affidavit filed last week, Love and Chan conspired to create fake financial documents that appeared to show they had earned millions of dollars via investments they never made. Love would allegedly find women online and attempt to convince them to send money to him or Chan, who he claimed was his financial advisor. Love allegedly told the women that Chan had a secret investment algorithm that had made him more than $30 million.

A core part of the scheme, investigators said, was that Love presented himself to victims as an active 49ers wide receiver to project the image that he was wealthy. Court documents show screenshots of Instagram posts Love allegedly made in which he donned 49ers equipment while pretending to train, at one point faking a contract signing for a video. In other cases, Love stole posts from actual NFL players and posted them as his own.

“Some victims became suspicious of Love and searched for Love’s information through the Internet,” the affidavit said. “Due to Love’s false social media representations, search engines and artificial intelligence occasionally stated that Love was a bona fide 49ers player. In January 2026, investigators entered Love’s first and last name in search engines and found that results did, in fact, sometimes depict Love as a player for the 49ers.”

Both the NFL and the 49ers told authorities Love had no connection to them. Attorneys for Love and Chan were not immediately available to comment when contacted Friday.

The affidavit said Love used a variety of aliases to conceal his true identity, at times posing as Green Bay Packers quarterback Jordan Love or claiming the two were related. His other alleged aliases included Jon Love and Avril Lyto Love. He also told some women he was a real estate investor from a wealthy Swiss family.

“Love spent over $1,160 at Green Gridiron, a website specializing in custom football helmets. Love purchased from Prop Money Inc., a company which sells realistic fake money for movies. Love also made purchases from Useviral.com and Buzzoid, companies that sell followers, likes, and views for social media accounts,” the affidavit said. “Investigators believe these purchases were made to enhance Love’s online appearance and alleged social standing in furtherance of the scheme.”

In many cases, Love allegedly developed romantic relationships with the women while telling them he wanted to invest with them so they could build lives together. He would then use apps such as Fake Bank Account Pro, which allow users to create fake bank accounts. Privately, he mocked them with Chan, who was 14 when the scheme began, and complained about having to maintain those relationships.

One victim, identified in the documents as A.T., said she dated Love for nearly a year before realizing she was being scammed. The affidavit said she lost more than $87,000 to Love and Chan via fake investments and vehicle leases she paid for, among other things. Another, identified as G.H., said Love threatened her with physical violence when she refused to send him her savings.

When other targets said they didn’t have enough money for Love’s supposed investments, he allegedly pressured them to take out personal loans that he left them unable to pay. Love would then block the victims and keep the stolen money. Authorities said they found no evidence Love had any legitimate source of income.

FBI agents arrested Love and Chan at the Boise Airport in Idaho while they were allegedly on their way to meet with new targets. The bureau is requesting anyone else potentially impacted by the scheme to come forward, as it “believes there are many more victims.”

articles.title: Five Things I Like: Week 13
articles.excerpt: Candace Pedraza breaks down five key storylines following week thirteen WNBA action.
articles.content:

Five Things I Like: Week 13

We are six days away from the start of the WNBA’s FIBA Women’s World Cup break, which means two things: there will be a pause on WNBA games until September 17 from that point on, and we’ll be catching the league’s stars competing on an international stage with international bragging rights at stake. 

So, we won’t really be all that deprived of a bit of WNBA action, albeit under the guise of watching powerhouses like the United States, France, Belgium, Japan, and others compete for the cup. 

With just over a week left until that break, though, the WNBA was chock-full of moments worth reliving.

Kuier Continues to Shine for Dallas

While Jessica Shepard has been getting a ton of praise for her ascension as a star big while with the Wings this season, Kuier has been an unsung hero on defense for Dallas as they struggle to find consistent rim protection. Her defense, coupled with her capabilities as a stretch 4, has made her a very fun bench piece for head coach Jose Fernandez to plug and play. 

Against the Indiana Fever in a game crucial to Dallas’ seeding, Kuier managed to rack up seven blocks, 11 points, eight boards, and four assists. She also hit two three-pointers to boot. 

After the game, Fever head coach Stephanie White tipped her hat to Kuier and the entire Wings front court, saying, “They have great length.… They did a great job of shelling us, forcing us into a crowd, and not allowing us to see some easy, open teammates. We got to watch the film, and we got to be better.”

Dallas is projected to face off against the Minnesota Lynx in round one of the playoffs if the season ended today. However, postseason seeding is far from settled beyond perhaps the Lynx at 1 and the Golden State Valkyries at 2. If they did face Minnesota, having depth like Kuier to back up Shepard is critical against the Lynx, who boast Natasha Howard next to Napheesa Collier in their frontcourt.

Bueckers’ Perfect Game from 3-point Range

Paige Bueckers #5 of the Dallas Wings

Remaining on the Dallas hype train for a moment, they finished up their weekend with a win over the last-place Seattle Storm. It was a blowout for essentially the entire contest, namely because Paige Bueckers didn’t miss from three-point range. She finished up the game with six threes and 32 total points. 18 of those points came in the 1st quarter.

Bueckers remains the tone setter for the Wings’ offense, while players like Arike Ogunbowale, Shepard, and Kuier contribute around her. With Azzi Fudd out for the year, it’s imperative that they find their offense from everywhere, and not just from three-point range. 

Still, it’s always cool to see a heater like this from Bueckers, who is looking to reach the postseason with the Wings for the first time since getting drafted last year. She has to remain as efficient as possible for the remaining stretch of games that Dallas has in front of them, and luckily for them, they have the second-easiest remaining strength of schedule in the WNBA.

Mitchell Continues to Crawl Up Leaderboard

As you might know, Las Vegas Aces superstar center A’ja Wilson is attempting to win her third straight scoring title this season. She’s at 935 points through August 24, but she has unbelievably stiff competition from Indiana Fever guard Kelsey Mitchell. She’s sitting at 967 total points scored through August 24, which means we could see two WNBA players finish up with over 1,000 points scored in a single season. 

Focusing on Mitchell, though, she continued her streak of scoring over 20 points per game this week. She’s upped her points per game average to 24.8, which is a career high. Mitchell, of course, didn’t draw too much attention to the fact that she broke Wilson’s previous record for the number of consecutive 20+ point games after the Fever’s loss to the Wings:

“But I think ultimately it just comes down, obviously, to work. But I don’t really take statistics really that serious. So a lot of this stuff is really circumstantial to me. So I [want] to get the dub, and we didn’t get that. So I think keep my focus on the right thing; keeping the main thing the main thing is important.” 

Mitchell is sneakily climbing into this year’s MVP conversation with this level of production, all of which is the best of her career.

Fiebich Returns with a Bang for New York

Leonie Fiebich #13 of the New York Liberty

While the New York Liberty have had a rough go of things this year, partially due to big injuries to Leonie Fiebich and Satou Sabally, they at least got some good news with the return of Fiebich to the floor ahead of the FIBA break. She immediately contributed on both ends of the floor for New York, posting 20 points, five boards, five assists, and a steal en route to a critical win against the Fever. 

Notably, she also held Clark to 2-7 shooting when she was her primary defender, per ESPN’s Alexa Phillipou. This, amid a hot scoring month for the point guard, is extremely encouraging for New York to see ahead of a potential postseason meet-up with Indiana. 

Fiebich is the kind of x-factor that a contending team like the Liberty needs to go on a deep postseason run. Wings do not grow on trees, and New York is sorely missing the length and defense that they get by plugging Fiebich back into the fold.

Reese Scores First 30-Point Performance

It was just one game, but it might be time to officially put to bed the notion that you can’t run your offense through Atlanta Dream forward Angel Reese. 

The third-year star recorded the first 30-point performance of her WNBA career against the Phoenix Mercury in a win. She shot 14-21 from the field, in addition to notching 14 rebounds, four steals, and two assists. 

This is huge for a few reasons, but mainly because Atlanta is better as a unit when Reese can put together huge games on offense like this one. Obviously, they have great weapons like Rhyne Howard and Allisha Gray around her. Still, one stat really proves why running some more offense through the third-year forward might be something to focus on: the Dream are 9-2 when she shoots 50 percent from the field or better this season, and just 15-11 when she does not, per CBS Sports’ Jack Maloney. 

Watching this specific game back, you see the potential for this kind of offense – the give-and-go between Reese and basically any of Atlanta’s guards, but especially players like Gray or Howard who have a lot of shooting gravity, is a great means of getting her open as a cutter. She can also use her strength in the post, which is what she did a lot of in this game. Her strengths as a ball handler also make her a threat as a bit of a quarterback keeper, to put it clunkily, as she can fake an outlet pass while running right to the paint for a shot. 

This makes Atlanta scary to face in the postseason and makes the prospect of having to defend Reese even scarier.

articles.title: Can Valkyries overtake Lynx’s top playoff seed? Our WNBA playoff picture forecast
articles.excerpt: There's an intriguing race for the top seed, while on the flip side, get ready for other teams to tank.
articles.content:
Latest

From WNBA

The Valkyries' end-of-season schedule looks ideal for them to keep pushing for a top seed. Elsa / Getty Images

Take a deep breath. After a fast and furious August featuring last-second game-winners, record-breaking performances and a little too much spiciness on and off the court, the WNBA will press pause for the next 16 days for the FIBA World Cup.

With four games remaining for each team during the regular season, let’s take a look at where we stand.

Playoff field is set

There hasn’t been much intrigue for weeks as to which teams will advance to the postseason, and the Dallas Wings ended any drama by clinching the final playoff spot last week. Although the Phoenix Mercury, Chicago Sky, Los Angeles Sparks and — to some extent — the expansion Portland Fire and Toronto Tempo harbored postseason hopes entering the 2026 season, the eight playoff teams this year will be the Atlanta Dream, Wings, Golden State Valkyries, Indiana Fever, Las Vegas Aces, Minnesota Lynx, New York Liberty and Washington Mystics.

Those team names were listed in alphabetical order with the seeding order still dramatically in flux. As indicated in The Athletic’s playoff projection bracket, the top three seeds are relatively certain: The Lynx are the odds-on favorite (94 percent likelihood) to secure the No. 1 seed, the Valkyries are in position to be the No. 2 seed, and the Aces are right behind them. Beyond that, no team has more than a 40 percent chance of landing at any particular slot. In fact, one of the most curious findings in the projection bracket is that the Dream are the most likely team to finish fourth and fifth, but they obviously can’t play each other in the first round of the postseason.

With so much at stake in the final four games of the season, every game between playoff teams takes on greater importance. Golden State, Las Vegas and Dallas are free and clear of any more postseason previews, but here are the six remaining:

Friday, Sept. 18: New York at Minnesota

Sunday, Sept. 20: Washington at Indiana

Monday, Sept. 21: Atlanta at New York

Tuesday, Sept. 22: Minnesota at Indiana

Wednesday, Sept. 23: Atlanta at New York

Thursday, Sept. 24: Indiana at Minnesota

The Lynx need to win at least one of those games (assuming they also beat the Connecticut Sun) to secure the No. 1 seed and homecourt advantage through the playoffs. Three wins could get New York into the top four and a first-round Game 1 at Barclays Center, and Atlanta probably needs to split with the Liberty to stay in the 4-5 matchup.

Several tiebreakers remain in flux. Indiana’s tiebreakers against New York, Washington and the Dream all have yet to be decided, so there will be no rest before the playoffs tip off.

Who is the championship favorite?

The Lynx have been the top seed for most of the season but head into the break losers of two in a row with Olivia Miles nicked up yet again. She also just had only the second zero assist game of her career, the first coming in a 32-point blowout over Toronto that was a little less consequential.

Minnesota is not nearly as bulletproof as one would expect a top seed to be. Since the All-Star break, the Lynx have the league’s second-best record, but only the fourth-best net rating. Their offense was bottled up against Golden State and their defense suffered against Atlanta. Leaks have been springing for some time in Minnesota.

Perhaps it’s not a surprise, then, that the Lynx have been usurped as the title favorite, per our projection bracket. That honor now goes to the Valkyries, coming off a week when they won on the road in Minnesota and New York. Golden State’s defense has been phenomenal all year, and their offense has perked up lately, in part thanks to the drives of Tiffany Hayes. No one can keep her out of the paint.

The Valkyries would be a unique title winner. It’s rare for a WNBA champion to be without a single no-brainer MVP candidate. In the last 17 years, only the 2021 Sky didn’t have a first-team All-WNBA player.

Maybe the Aces should still be considered a title favorite with their prodigious top-end talent. Even without NaLyssa Smith, Las Vegas has a roster full of proven playoff performers, a head coach with a 10-1 record in playoff series and A’ja Wilson, who is the best player alive. Then again, if the Aces matched up with the Liberty in the first round, an early exit against a team that can take advantage of its lack of size wouldn’t exactly be surprising.

The Fever have the best offense in WNBA history, and this league has historically rewarded offense over defense. Kelsey Mitchell and Caitlin Clark can go on heaters that many other teams can’t keep up with, but Indiana’s offense can sometimes be bogged down by full-court pressure.

I tend to believe there is no championship favorite at this point. Expansion of the league by 25 percent in the last two seasons has created a little too much parity, giving several teams an opportunity to emerge victorious this postseason.

Prepare for an epic tank-off

The pandemic years are long behind us, but the issue of college eligibility hasn’t yet been settled. The NCAA’s new five-in-five rule means that the 2027 draft class won’t be decided until much closer to April, since all of the best prospects can choose to return to college for one more season.

The uncertainty of who could be available hasn’t stopped several franchises from, let’s just say, incentivizing their odds of landing a top pick by accumulating as many losses as possible. As a result, the lottery standings are almost as compelling as the playoff race.

Four games remain between a pair of non-playoff teams, and two of them stand out. The first is on Sept. 20 between Portland and Los Angeles. Neither team has let go of the rope to end the season; both collected surprising wins against playoff-bound opponents last week and have looked a cut better than the rest of their lottery-destined peers. To wit: Carla Leite proved wholly deserving of her first invite to a major senior tournament for France by dropping 26 points and six assists in a rout over Atlanta. Meanwhile, Nneka Ogwumike looks like she could command a multi-year max contract in free agency despite just announcing her retirement.

The Fire and Sparks are in fifth and sixth position in the lottery standings, but they could flip if Portland wins at Los Angeles. Neither spot has a great chance of securing the No. 1 pick, but the odds from fifth-place are about twice as good. The main reason to pick the Sparks in this particular matchup is that Ogwumike has been vocal about her desire to play the right way to close out the season, and coach Lynne Roberts has said that finishing strong — despite the potential harm to the Sparks’ lottery odds — is the best way to honor the franchise legend. Considering L.A.’s only other home game after the break is against Golden State, this might be the best opportunity to send Ogwumike out in style.

The other truly tanktastic matchup comes on the last day of the regular season between Connecticut and Toronto. The Sun have been on a methodical two-year teardown, and the fruit of their labor would be top odds for the No. 1 pick in the 2027 draft. On the other hand, the Tempo were seemingly angling for a playoff bid in 2026 but pivoted due to a rash of injuries. As an expansion team, this is the only opportunity for team to execute a one-year tank, and Toronto has worked its way to the bottom, winning one of its last 17 games. Good luck recognizing all of the players in the lineups that the Tempo are putting out: In their latest miserable loss to Phoenix, three of their bench players weren’t even in camp to start the season.

It’s possible that the two teams might enter the final day with Toronto needing one more loss to tie Connecticut for the worst two-year win percentage, which would result in splitting the top odds. And the poor Sun will be saying goodbye to Connecticut on a day when a win would be the worst thing that could happen to them.

articles.title: Caitlin Clark and Angel Reese must now work together at Women's World Cup as WNBA takes a high-stakes break
articles.excerpt: Caitlin Clark and Angel Reese must set aside their WNBA rivalry and build team chemistry as Team USA defends its title at the Women's Basketball World Cup in Berlin.
articles.content:
Caitlin Clark and Angel Reese's chemistry, and what happens during the national anthem are key questions for the US

Jackson Thompson Exposes the WNBA’s Biggest Problem

OutKick Reporter Jackson Thompson joins Riley Gaines to break down what he’s seeing inside the WNBA’s biggest cultural moment. Riley and Jackson discuss Caitlin Clark, Sophie Cunningham, the Indiana Fever, WNBA fan energy, league growth, media gatekeeping, and whether the league is prepared for its expanding audience. They also discuss the ongoing debate over men in women’s sports, questions around WNBA eligibility policies, Enes Kanter Freedom, Royce White, San Jose State volleyball, and how sports media has covered female athletes speaking out. Plus, Jackson shares what he’s watching next as the WNBA postseason approaches and Team USA women’s basketball prepares for international competition.

The U.S. is headed to a battle in Berlin.

Caitlin Clark and Angel Reese will have to work together to uphold American dominance in the Women's Basketball World Cup in September. At home, the WNBA will take a two-week break from hosting the chaos of the 2026 season.

So Americans will have to root together for their biggest stars on the world stage. The U.S. has won four consecutive World Cups in a row and this year's team will also have to protect an active 30-game win streak.

What happens in Berlin could very well shape the climate of the league that the players return to when the WNBA season resumes.

 

Can Clark and Reese work together?

Angel Reese and Caitlin Clark of the USA Women's National Team look on during a game against Puerto Rico during the 2026 FIBA World Cup Qualifying Tournament on March 12, 2026, at Coliseo Jose Miguel Agrelot in San Juan, Puerto Rico. (NBAE via Getty Images)

Clark and Reese have spent more than three years framed as adversaries.

The last time they were on a basketball court, Clark was seen laughing as she walked by Reese, who had just missed the game-winning layup.

Their rivalry fueled the 2023 national championship game between Iowa and LSU. It followed them into a rematch in the 2024 NCAA Tournament, then into the WNBA as the top two contenders for Rookie of the Year. Every matchup, foul and postgame comment became another invitation for fans to choose a side.

But at times, they've also shown glimpses of what that can look like when playing together.

Reese first said, "one day, hopefully, we can be teammates," while discussing Clark in an October 2024 Wall Street Journal article.

They first became teammates at the 2024 WNBA All-Star Game, when Clark recorded 10 assists and Reese finished with 12 points and 11 rebounds in Team WNBA’s victory over the U.S. Olympic team.

CAITLIN CLARK HELPS WNBA SHATTER ANOTHER TV RATINGS RECORD AS FEVER-DREAM DRAWS MASSIVE AUDIENCE

In March, Clark and Reese helped the U.S. go 5-0 at the World Cup qualifying tournament in Puerto Rico.

There was an awkward moment when Clark appeared to ignore a high five invitation from Reese during one of the games.

Clark earned tournament MVP honors after averaging 11.6 points and a tournament-leading 6.4 assists. Reese averaged a team-high eight rebounds while shooting 52.2% from the field.

"Team chemistry is everything," Reese said during the qualifying tournament. "Some of us have played with each other on our respective teams, but we have to come together and find your role. Everybody’s not going to be able to do everything that they do on their respective team."

Clark and Reese will play alongside established champions A’ja Wilson, Breanna Stewart, Napheesa Collier and Chelsea Gray in Berlin.

 

What will happen during the national anthems?

Team Coop stands for the national anthem before the 2026 WNBA All-Star Game at the United Center in Chicago. (NBAE via Getty Images)

The available rules and national-team precedent point to the entire U.S. team standing on the court for "The Star-Spangled Banner" in Berlin. Whether every player places her hand over her heart or sings along is a separate question that neither USA Basketball nor FIBA rules answer.

The issue has drawn new attention during the 2026 WNBA season because teams have followed different routines.

Several WNBA teams historically and routinely remain in the locker room or clear the floor during the playing of the national anthem as part of pregame routines.

CHINA’S INFLUENCE MACHINE: FEDERAL RECORDS EXPOSE BEIJING’S PUSH TO SWAY AMERICA

The Atlanta Dream remained in their locker room while the anthem played before their Aug. 16 game against the Indiana Fever. That left Reese and Rhyne Howard, both members of the World Cup roster, off the court while Clark, Aliyah Boston and the rest of the Fever stood along the sideline.

Clark stood facing the flag with her hands behind her back. Sophie Cunningham placed her right hand over her heart.

The difference generated criticism of Clark online, although nothing in the WNBA rulebook requires players to sing or place a hand over their heart.

Sophie Cunningham and Caitlin Clark of the Indiana Fever stand for the national anthem before a game against the Chicago Sky at United Center in Chicago, Ill., on Aug. 8, 2026. (Getty Images)

The rules change when those players leave their WNBA teams and join the national program.

USA Basketball’s code of conduct requires participants to follow FIBA and USA Basketball rules, attend team functions as directed and "demonstrate proper respect during the playing of the national anthem." The code does not define "proper respect," but it gives USA Basketball authority to investigate alleged violations and impose discipline.

FIBA also controls the ceremonies in Berlin. Its 2026 regulations state that only anthems and flags of countries or national federations recognized by FIBA may be used. The regulations leave the details of World Cup ceremonies to the tournament’s hosting documents. They do not publicly prescribe whether a player must sing, place a hand over her heart or assume another specific posture.

FIBA’s code of conduct additionally prohibits players and other "basketball parties" from using gestures, words or objects to transmit political or ideological messages that are deemed unfit for a sporting event. The rule does not specifically identify kneeling, remaining silent or declining to place a hand over the heart as violations. It does, however, give FIBA greater control over demonstrations than the WNBA has exercised during its domestic season.

Past U.S. teams have treated international competition differently from the WNBA. American players who routinely remained off the court during WNBA anthems stood together for them at the 2021 Tokyo Olympics. Sue Bird, then the team’s captain and now the managing director who selected the 2026 roster, said wearing a USA uniform changed the context.

"You are wearing USA jerseys and it does change the conversation a little bit and what you’re representing," Bird said at the time. "With that, I don’t feel like a hypocrite in any way. Everyone knows where we stand. I don’t think it contradicts anything since we’re actually doing the work." The U.S. players stood with their arms linked during that Olympic run.

There also were no reported anthem protests during the United States’ five-game World Cup qualifying run in Puerto Rico in March. That team included Clark, Reese, Howard, Paige Bueckers and Kahleah Copper.

As of Aug. 30, no member of the World Cup roster has publicly announced plans to kneel, leave the floor or conduct another demonstration during the anthem in Berlin.

 

Rival world powers collide

articles.title: JD Vance set to address Jewish conservatives, as some Jews in GOP share concerns about his recent Israel remarks
articles.excerpt: Vice President JD Vance is set to address a gathering of Jewish conservatives on Monday, even as some Jews in the GOP have raised concerns about his remarks on Israel.
articles.content:
Some Jews in GOP say his attendance at the event is a positive sign.

Vice President JD Vance is set to address a major gathering of Jewish conservatives on Monday, with some Jews in the GOP raising concerns that the vice president is breaking with them on Israel -- and others saying his attendance at the event is a positive sign.

Vance is set to speak at the Republican Jewish Coalition (RJC) annual leadership summit in Las Vegas, Nevada, just hours after a campaign stop in Michigan.

But while the RJC is staunchly supportive of Israel, the vice president has made sharp and skeptical comments toward Israel in recent months, contrasting with the party faithful's traditionally supportive line toward the Jewish state.

While delivering a press briefing in the White House in June, for instance, as the United States was working on a deal to pause the war started by the U.S. and Israel with Iran, Vance told reporters that he had seen Israeli Cabinet members criticize the deal and would tell them that "Donald J. Trump is the only head of state in the entire world who is sympathetic to the nation of Israel at this moment in time ... If I was in the Cabinet of the Israeli government, I might not be attacking the only powerful ally that I have anywhere left in the entire world."

In a later interview with podcaster Joe Rogan, Vance also said that "there are some people" in the Israeli government "we know beyond a shadow of a doubt who are manipulating and trying to change American public opinion to keep the war going on indefinitel. ... what I would say to the Americans who sort of see this and are frustrated by it, my attitude would be: you should be frustrated at American leaders who are persuaded by this, affected by this."

Vance also said other governments run similar influence campaigns. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu later told ABC News he spoke with Vance about those comments "and I think we straightened that out because we're not. That's not our policy."

Vance, in a later Fox News interview where he was asked about reported discordant conversations with Netanyahu, said that Israel is "a great partner" but that he was willing to have "a frank conversation" with Netanyahu when their viewpoints differ, similar to conversations with other U.S. allies.

Maura Schrier-Fleming, who is a member of a Dallas-based group of Jewish Republican women, told ABC News that she found some of Vance's comments about Israel's actions in the region to be "a mischaracterization of how Israel has had to defend itself."

Asked what she'd be looking to hear from Vance at the conference, Schrier-Fleming said, "He's got to emphasize that what's good for America is good for Americans, and our ally, our only democratic ally in the Middle East, has demonstrated to America that they are worth more than the aid we provide them."

A veteran Republican operative, who asked not to be named as he is actively working in Republican politics, pointed to Vance's White House briefing as an inflection point to how Vance has been discussed among Jewish Republicans, saying that Vance's support among Jewish conservatives collapsed tremendously after he said that.

The operative felt that further efforts by Vance to reach out to Jewish conservatives or to show support for Israel was akin to an "apology tour," as well as a calculation toward winning back support among the Jewish right ahead of a potential run for president in 2028. Vance has declined to confirm if he plans to run for the presidency in 2028, saying he is focused on the midterms, but has left the door open to a run.

Both Vance and Trump have aired disagreements with Netanyahu, with the president confirming to Axios in mid-June that he had excoriated Netanyahu over a strike in Lebanon.

In the Fox interview, Vance also framed his dissent with Israel as part of a partnership with the ally, saying, "When our interests are aligned with Israel, we talk about how to accomplish those shared objectives. When my viewpoint is averse to the Prime Minister of Israel, we have a frank conversation about that."

Beyond discussions of Israel, Vance has also condemned antisemitism on numerous occasions, allaying other potential concerns of Jewish conservatives.

Some Jewish conservatives have pushed back on the notion that there's any divide between Vance and Jewish Republicans on Israel.

David Scharf, an attorney who is a major donor to Republicans, told ABC News by email that he recently spoke with Vance "about shared themes in Judaism and Catholicism," and that "as for Israel, I can speak from my own interactions with him, where he has been unequivocal in expressing support for the U.S.-Israel alliance."

Some Republican Jewish conservatives have also said they feel the fact that Vance is going to the RJC in the first place is a positive sign that he wants to reconnect with Jewish conservatives and to have conversations about Israel.

Eric Levine, a major fundraiser for GOP Senate candidates, told ABC News, "The fact that he's coming to speak to us, I think, is a very good thing."

Levine is a board member of the RJC, but spoke to ABC News in a personal capacity, not on behalf of the organization.

"The fact that he's coming to speak to us, I think, is a very good thing. He's reaching out to the Jewish community... and not just the Jewish community, but anyone who supports the American-Israeli relationship and wants to fight antisemitism," Levine said.

articles.title: “John Galliano: Horizons,” The Met’s Spring 2027 Costume Institute Exhibition, Will Not Proceed as Planned
articles.excerpt: After much reflection and discussion with The Met and all those involved, John Galliano has decided that it is best for the exhibition not to take place at this time.
articles.content:
The Metropolitan Museum of Art, together with John Galliano, announced this morning that the Spring 2027 exhibition devoted to his four-decade oeuvre will not proceed as planned.

The show—which was to encompass garments, accessories, sketches, toiles, research books, and archival materials stretching across Galliano’s career, from his “Les Incroyables” Central Saint Martins graduate collection of 1984 to his work for the Paris couture houses Givenchy and Dior to his final blockbuster show for Maison Margiela—would have been only the third retrospective of a living designer at the Costume Institute, following Yves Saint Laurent in 1983 and Comme des Garcons’s Rei Kawakubo in 2017.

The July 31, 2026, announcement of the exhibition received mixed reactions. Few designers’ work is as universally admired at Galliano’s, so within the fashion community there was great excitement, however local political and civic leaders raised concerns.

John Galliano stated: “I am profoundly grateful to The Metropolitan Museum of Art, and particularly to Max Hollein, Andrew Bolton, and Anna Wintour, for the extraordinary honour of proposing an exhibition devoted to my work. To have my creative journey considered by an institution that I have admired throughout my life moved me more deeply than I can express. I will remain forever grateful for the confidence, care and scholarship that Max, Andrew, Anna and the entire Met team brought to this project.”

He continued, “After much reflection and discussion with The Met and all those involved, I have decided, with great sadness, that it is best for the exhibition not to take place at this time. I remain fully accountable for the pain caused by my words in the past, particularly the hurt I caused to the Jewish and Asian communities, and I remain deeply sorry for it. I understand that meaningful atonement is not achieved through an exhibition, institutional recognition or a single public gesture. It is a continuing responsibility, demonstrated through listening, learning and one’s conduct over time.”

“I do not want the debate surrounding me to place The Met in a difficult position or to distract from the remarkable work of the Costume Institute,” he went on. “I also recognize and respect that an exhibition honouring my work would be painful for some. I would also like to express my deepest gratitude to all those who have guided, supported and accompanied me throughout these fifteen years of sobriety and recovery from alcoholism and addiction. Your wisdom, patience and humanity have helped me more than I can ever adequately express. I remain profoundly indebted to you for giving me, as you promised, a life better than I could ever have dreamt of. My gratitude to the Met, Max, Andrew and Anna remains profound and enduring. Their generosity, humanity and belief in the importance of fashion as art, culture and history, as well as their understanding of human fragility and the possibility of growth, will remain with me always.”

Max Hollein, Director and CEO of The Metropolitan Museum of Art, said: “Following thoughtful discussions with many stakeholders and with John Galliano, we together have decided not to proceed with the exhibition.”

In the statement, Anna Wintour said, “John’s decision to ask the Museum to postpone the exhibition devoted to his work is very courageous and a measure of the man he is. I believe this is the right decision, and both he and the Museum have my full support. His soaring imagination, fed by a lifetime of curiosity and research, is matched by his exceptional craft. Cut, fit, the evocative line of a bias-cut dress, color—he’s a master of it all. Without one or the other, if his technique wasn’t equal to his storytelling talents, he wouldn’t be the premiere couturier of his generation. But he most certainly is. From the staged-on-a-shoestring feat that was his Fall 1994 show at the Sao Schlumberger Hotel Particulier in Paris to his tour de force swansong at Maison Margiela Artisanal for Spring 2024, Galliano gave fashion its most marvelous shows. The way that Christian Dior called Cristobal Balenciaga “the master of us all,” a generation of designers have looked to Galliano as the greatest. His impact reverberates across generations, not least of all with Dior’s current creative director Jonathan Anderson, who calls Galliano one of his heroes.”

Information on a new Spring Costume Institute exhibition and the 2027 Met Gala will be announced at a later date.

A drone’s five-day intrusion over a restricted US missile range triggered an unusually broad response and raised questions about hidden surveillance.

In spring 2025, U.S. agencies intercepted a quadcopter that had violated the restricted airspace over White Sands Missile Range in New Mexico for approximately five days. The drone’s flight path suggested it may have been conducting reconnaissance of the military facility.

The operation involved the U.S. Army, the Federal Bureau of Investigation, the Department of Homeland Security, and the Pentagon unit that analyzes unidentified anomalous phenomena. Electronic warfare measures forced the drone to land in a parking lot.

A Camper Van and Chinese Nationals Near a Military Base

At the same time, law enforcement officers were monitoring several Chinese nationals near White Sands. They arrived in the United States, rented a Mercedes camper van, and drove across the country to the missile range.

Separately, officials identified a Chinese woman who drove a rental car to White Sands National Park and remained there after it closed. The group in the camper van was detained by military personnel and later handed over to federal authorities. The woman was fined and released.

Helicopters and a Drone Chase Over White Sands

The incident in spring 2025 was not the first time a suspicious drone had appeared over the military facility. In the fall of 2024, border agents pursued a similar drone over White Sands for about 56 kilometers, deploying helicopters and their own unmanned aircraft.

After the aircraft crossed the border into Mexico, the pursuit was called off. U.S. officials emphasize that not all illegal drone flights show signs of espionage. Drones are also launched by hobbyists, tourists, and criminal groups, which may use them to transport drugs.

Laser Systems Against Drones and Risks for the United States

The availability of inexpensive drones has made protecting U.S. military bases and critical infrastructure a separate challenge. For a long time, no agency had clearly defined responsibility for responding to such threats.

Following a series of incidents, U.S. Northern Command began coordinating responses to small drones appearing over military bases. The Pentagon is expanding its arsenal of countermeasures, including laser systems, high-powered microwave systems, and electronic warfare tools.

At the same time, the use of such technologies has already caused problems. In February, the airspace over El Paso was closed because of a poorly coordinated test of a laser system. Later, the military mistakenly shot down a U.S. Customs and Border Protection drone with a laser.

New Powers to Combat Drones

In 2026, the U.S. Congress expanded the powers of the Central Intelligence Agency, state authorities, and local police to force down drones that may threaten critical sites.

Counterintelligence specialists acknowledge that establishing a direct link between a specific drone flight and Chinese intelligence services is extremely difficult. In 2024, Chinese national Yinpiaо Zhou was detained for flying a drone over Vandenberg Space Force Base during the launch of a military satellite.

Zhou was sentenced to four months in federal prison for violating restricted airspace rules. U.S. officials believe that drone defense systems are gradually improving, but military facilities and critical infrastructure in the United States remain vulnerable.
